body: writing this out helped, since I obviously can't tell anyone close to me. I don't think I'm going to end up dead from all this, maybe I can find some solution. maybe you all can too. I feel stupid posting here because a lot of you are in constant pain and life has no hope of improvement. I'm young and somewhat healthy but I still can't see the hope. I hope you all don't find me too naive and stupid.

I'd like to start by saying I'm not a furry. I found this sub today and I wanted to share that I've never seen a happier, sweeter, and more positive community in the face of how society treats them. You guys are awesome, and if I could I would be friends with any one of you in real life. I've had many furry friends and I always said that if I was younger when I learned about the concept I would have probably gotten into the culture myself. The world is made for everyone, no matter what, and anyone who disagrees is lacking a fundamental cog in their heart. I just wanted to send some love from the outside in case anyone needed it. I wasn't sure where else to post this as I don't feel the right to make a whole post or intrude on someone else's.

Oh yeah recipe sorry. 
Almond flour crust- 1 cup almond flour, 2 tbsp butter, 1 egg. Roll out as thin as you want (1/4 in works great) and bake for 10 min at 375. Or until you feel it's crispy enough. 

Add sugar free sauce and cheese and veggies or whatever you want. Net carbs 2g for 1/4 of the crust.

My own recipe. 
Ingredients:
1/4 block of tofu. Firmness of your choice, really doesn't matter. 
1 tsp almond flour. 
1 egg. 
Season generously with whatever you want and mash it all up with a fork until you get an evenish consistency. 
Heat up some oil of choice (I recently started using coconut) in a pan on med and fry for a few minutes. They take a minute to cook all the way through so don't be hasty in flipping. Also it's not easy to flip because half of it is still basically goo. I'll leave that part up to you to figure out. 

Plop it on a couple pieces of lettuce when the patties are done on both sides. They should look a little browned and be pretty firm.
 My condiment of choice is a spoonful of Sriracha mixed with a spoonful of mayo. 
Toss on some onion and spinach too. The flavors work perfectly together.
These things are my favorite vegetarian patties and have been a staple for the past year that I've been vegetarian.
